attempt_deadlines.description: Paykit wire 4.5, Paykit spec 7.1, wire 6.2: the deadline an attempt carries, d + 1 ms. For a one-time request d is the earlier of proposal_expires_at and the payment deadline's timestamp; for a Billing Period it is the period's start plus the payment deadline's seconds; with neither the attempt carries no deadline (null). d is read at millisecond precision, further digits truncated (wire 1.6), and the deadline is written with three fraction digits. Each case names a request of messages.json, or gives the two fields of a one-time request.

description: Every operation type (wire 6.1-6.4) for alice's account at generation 1, signed by its writer over lp("pubky-switch/v1/op", identity, body). Signer operations carry app_id null. Batches share one batch ID and count; cursor.set is unsigned and outside the count. Each record.put value opens with alice's scope key to a record value of Paykit wire 5.

integer_bounds.description: Wire 1.1: every int is a JSON number from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (9007199254740991), without sign, fraction or exponent. Each case is the operation named in based_on with its orphan_after written as number, signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the integer rule decides: the largest integer is valid; 2^53, a fraction (86400.0 included), an exponent and a sign are refused with 400 bad_request, before the operation's fields are read. Only the opaque members wire 1.1 names by path are exempt: a message body's metadata, a payment proof body's proof, an invite code's context (encoding.json json).

ops_request.note: POST /v1/{id}/ops body of the registration batch (wire 6.4, spec 12.1 step 2): app.put and the first receive_key.put, then the cursor.

unknown member beside cursor.set's op and position

batch_entries.description: Wire 1.1, 2.2, 6.4: an entry of a POST /ops body has only its own members: a signed operation's carrying form body and sig, a cursor.set its op and position. Each case is the body of ops_request with the member future_restriction added to the entry at the path in member, so every signature still verifies and only the member check refuses it: 400 bad_request, before any signature is checked.

unknown_members.description: Wire 1.1, 6.1: unknown members are refused at every depth of an operation body, as at its top level: in batch, a condition and its object, expected_version, value_sealed, id_inputs, the carrying form of a signed record or cert, and the key bundle. Each case is the operation named in based_on with the member future_restriction added at the path in member (a dotted path; numbers index arrays), signed again by its writer, so its signature verifies and only the member check refuses it: 400 bad_request. The opaque context of invite_code.put is exempt.
